sources.text: JERVOIS, LIEUT.-GEN. SIR WILLIAM FRANCIS DRUMMOND, G.C.M.G. (1878), (K.C.M.G., 1874), C.B., R.E., F.R.S.—Served at the Cape of Good Hope, 1841 until 1848, of which time he was six years on the frontier and in Kaffraria. In 1842 he was brigade-major to an expedition against the Dutch Boers; served in Kaffir war of 1846-7, and made map of British Kaffraria. From 1852 to 1855 was specially employed at Alderney in the fortification of that island; from 1856 to 1875 was on the staff of the war office as assistant inspector-general of fortifications, and subsequently as deputy-director of fortifications. From 1857 to 1875 was secretary of the committee on the defence of the empire, and in 1859 secretary to the royal commission on national defences; whilst in war office, carried out fortifications at Portsmouth, Plymouth, Pembroke, Portland, the Thames, Medway, and Cork; in 1863 was nominated a civil C.B.; in 1863 was sent to Canada, New Brunswick, Nova Scotia and Bermuda, to report on the defences of those provinces; and again in 1864, to confer with the Canadian government as to the defences of the dominion. His proposals were approved by the imperial and colonial authorities, and those for Bermuda and Halifax have been adopted and carried out; in 1865 was sent to Malta, and in 1866 to Gibraltar, to prepare projects for the improvement of the defences at those fortresses. He again visited Halifax and Bermuda in 1869, and made further reports on the defences; in 1871-2 was employed by the government of India to inspect and report upon the defences of Aden, Perim, Bombay, and the Hooghly. He also visited British Burmah, and subsequently submitted reports with regard to the defences of Rangoon and Moulmein. Governor of the Straite Settlements, 1875-7; successfully quelled insurrection of Malays in States of Perak and Sungei Ujong; prepared plan for government of protected Malay States; was selected by H.M.'s government to proceed to the Australian colonies to advise the respective governments regarding a scheme of defence for the Australian ports; governor, New Zealand. 1882-9, when he retired.

JERVOIS, LIEUT.-GEN. SIR WILLIAM FRANCIS DRUMMOND, G.C.M.G. (1884).—B. 1844; entered the army, 32nd lt. infy., Jan. 1862; capt., 1873; priv. sec. and A.D.C. to the offr. admnstng. the govt. of Mauritius from July, 1873, to Jan., 1874; ag. ch. civ. comsnr., Seychelles Is., from Apr., 1874, until Feb., 1875; mem. of the exec. and legis. couns. of Fiji, May, 1875; apptd. W. Africa Sttlmts., 1881; Apr., 1881, sent on a mission to Paris in conjunction with Mr. (now Sir A.) sources.text: CLARKE, WILLIAM JAMES.—Joined Natal Mounted Police, 1878; served through Zulu war, 1879 (medal with clasp); accompd. ex-Empress Eugenie on her tour through Natal and Zululand, 1880; served in Basutoland war, 1880 (medal with clasp); served in Transvaal campaign, 1881, present at battle of Laing's Nek; accompd. mission to Pondoland, 1887; with mission to Tongoland, under Col. Sir R. Martin, in 1888, and with the Portuguese-Swazi bdry. comsn., 1888; ag. res. mag. and admstr. of Native law for Ixopo div., 1889-90; apptd. crim. investign. offr., 1895; commanded Natal police field force on S. border during disturbances in E. Griqualand, 1897, and in Zululand, 1898; took part in Boer war, 1899-1902; commanded N.P. field force, in operations round Ladysmith, and during the siege; present at capture of Boer guns on Gun hill, and at battle of Caesar's Camp, on 6th Jan., 1900; with cav. brig. in attack on Botha's Pass, 1900; attached to the F.I.D.; was intell. offr. with Gen. Dartnell's column in the operations under Gen. French in E. Transvaal, and was sent by the latter gen. on spec. mis. to Zululand, 1901; joined Gen. Bullock's col. as intell. offr. in the E. Transvaal, 1901; ag. intell. offr. with General Dartnell's col. in O.R.C., 1901. In charge of sec. serv. dept. in Natal, 1902; sent by Gen. Bruce Hamilton on spec. mis. to Zululand, and was afterwards intell. offr. on that gen.'s staff, in the operations in S.E. Transvaal (medal with 4 clasps); accompd. the Prime Min. of Natal to England, in the capacity of sec., to attend the coronation, 1902; asst. comsnr., Natal pol., 1st Dec., 1904; ag. ch. comsnr., 1st Apr., 1905; served as chief of staff to Col. Mansel during Natal rebellion, 1906; ch. comsnr. of pol., 1st Nov., 1906; special duty in Transvaal to advise on re-organisation of S.A.C., 1906; commanded S. African police contingent at the coronation of H.M. King George V., in London, 1911.

sources.text: CRAWFORD, JAMES ADAIR, late Indian C.S.—Educ. at Rugby; apptd. after exam. of 1876; arrived, 17th Sept., 1878, and served in Bombay as asst. collr. and mag.; from Feb., 1881, served in the pol. dept., and acted as asst. to the agent for Rajputana, boundary settlt. officer in Mewar, and asst. to the resdnt. at Hyderabad; attaché, foreign dept., May, 1882; in charge of office of press commr., 1882-83; asst. commr., Ajmir, April, 1884; asst. sec., foreign dept., Jan., 1885; pol. agent, Quetta and Pishin, Nov., 1885; junr. under sec. to govt. foreign dept., March, 1888; acting first asst. and sec. for Berar to rest. at Hyderabad, May, 1890; under sec. to govt. of India, foreign dept., April, 1892; on special duty in connection with the revision of Aitchison's 'Treaties,' Oct., 1892; and again with the Archduke of Austria during his tour in India, 1892-93; offg. pol. rest., Persian Gulf, July-Dec., 1893; rest. and rev. commr., Baluchistan, March, 1895; commr., Berar, April, 1899; offg. resdnt., Mysore, and chief commr., Coorg, June, 1899, and May, 1901; ret'd. Aug., 1903.

FORD, CHARLES F.L.S.—Suptdt. Botanic Afforestation department, Hong Kong, 1871. 5th, 1862; 2nd secretary in Her Majesty's diplomatic service, Oct. 1st, 1862; chargé d'affaires at Carlsruhe from Oct. 15th, 1862, till Sept. 26th, 1864; transferred to Vienna, June 25th, 1864; sent to Buenos Ayres, Aug. 10th, 1865, where he was in charge of the mission from Dec. 1865, till Oct. 13th, 1866; transferred to Copenhagen, June 26th, 1866, where he was acting chargé d'affaires from Mar. 3rd till May 18th, 1867; sent to Washington, Mar. 28th, 1867, where he was acting chargé d'affaires from Sept. 1867, till Feb. 8th, 1868; secretary of embassy at Petersburg, Mar. 30th, 1871, where he was charged d'affaires from Nov. 16th, 1871, till 1872; transferred to Vienna, Oct. 26th, 1872; chargé d'affaires at Carlsruhe and Darmstadt, 11th, 1873; appointed Her Majesty's agent to attend the commission at Halifax, under the 22nd and 23rd Articles of the Treaty of Washington of 8th, 1871, July 26th, 1873; H.M.'s envoy ordinary and minister plenipotentiary to the United Mexican Republic, 22nd Feb., 1878; ditto to the Emperor of Brazil, 14th June 1879; ditto to the King of the Hellenes, 5th Mar., 1881; sent on special commission to Paris, and subsequently to Constantinople with Mr. Pennell of the colonial office in connection with the Newfoundland fisheries question, 1884; envoy extraordinary and plenipotentiary to the King of Spain, 1884; negotiated the commercial convention between Great Britain and Spain, signed, 1886; made a privy councillor, 1888; ambassador at Madrid, 1888; at Constantinople, 1892; at Rome, Comsn., Feb. to July, 1892; med. offr. special mission to Kumasi, Dec. 1894 to Jan. 1895; col. surg., Gambia, Feb., 1895.

sources.text: MARTINDALE, SIR ARTHUR HENRY TEMPLE, K.C.S.I., late Indian C.S. (Madras).—Educ. at Cheltenham Coll.; apptd. after exam. of 1873; arrived, 10th Nov., 1875; served in Madras as asst. collr. and mag., and in the foreign dept. of the govt. of India as attaché, and asst. and junr. under sec. to govt.; offg. asst. to rest. in Mysore and sec. to the chief commr. of Coorg, Feb., 1885; offg. rest., May–June, 1885; first asst. and sec. for Berar to the rest., Hyderabad, Nov., 1886; pol. agent, Quetta and Pishin, Apr., 1887; 1st asst. to govr.-gen.'s agent, Central India, Oct., 1888; pol. agent, Bhopal, July, 1890, and Jhalawar, Jan., 1892; on spl. duty in connection with the revision of Aitchison's "Treaties," Jan.–Apr., 1892; commr., Ajmer-Merwara, May, 1894; acting rest., W. states of Rajputana, June, 1895; agent to govr.-genl., Rajputana, and chief commr., Ajmer-Merwara, Mar., 1898; C.S.I., May, 1900; K.C.S.I., June, 1904; retd., Oct., 1905.

(1875), (KNIGHT BACHELOR (1859), (P.C., 1883).—Served for some time in the 87th Fusiliers; on his retirement from the army was actively engaged during the Irish famine, 1846-9, under the commission of public works and poor law board in Ireland; chief commissioner to inquire into the fair markets of Ireland, 1852; president of Munster, 1854; lieutenant-governor of St. Christopher, 1851; with which he held the dormant commission of governor-in-chief of the Leeward Islands; governor of Hong Kong, June, 1859. Was a member of the commission appointed in the autumn of 1863, to inquire into the financial condition of the Straits Settlements; governor of Ceylon, May, 1865; governor of New South Wales, 1872; employed on special service in 1874-5 in connection with the cession of the Fiji Islands to Great Britain; governor, New Zealand, 1877; governor of the Cape of Good Hope, Griqualand West, and H.M.'s high commissioner in South Africa, 1880; president of the Royal Commission on the settlement of the affairs of the Transvaal, 1881; governor of British Bechuanaland in conjunction with governorship of the Cape Colony, 1885; on special mission to Mauritius, Oct., 1886, when he assumed the government for a few days; resigned, 1889; reappointed 1895.

sources.text: WODEHOUSE, CHARLES, C.I.E., Colonel, I.S.C., Political Department, Bombay.—First commission, Bombay infantry, March, 1857; arrived in India, 6th April, 1857, and was employed under the military department, including service in the mutiny campaign, 1857-58 (medal and clasp for Central India); from March, 1867, served as boundary settlement commissioner, Baroda; from Sept., 1868, acted in the Hyderabad assigned districts as assistant commissioner, director of public instruction, and small cause court judge; acting assistant resident, Hyderabad, April to Nov., 1870; acting cantonment magistrate and judge, Secunderabad, Dec., 1870; acting assistant resident, Baroda, Jan., 1873; acting political agent, Rewa Kantha, Feb., 1873; from March, 1873, served in Kathiawar as political assistant, acting judicial assistant, and acting political agent, and was placed on special duty for the settlement of boundary disputes in the Gheer forest, July, 1874; also acted as private secretary to the governor of Bombay from May, 1876, to April, 1877; political agent, Mahi Kantha, Sept., 1881; 2nd grade, political agent, Feb., 1885; acting political superintendent, Palanpur, April, 1885, and in Kathiawar, July, 1886; C.I.E., Aug., 1887; on duty in England in connection with the Jubilee, 1887; political agent, Kolhapur, &c., Feb., 1889.

HOLLIS, Sir Alfred Claud, G.C.M.G. (1934), K.C.M.G. (1927), C.M.G. (1911), C.B.E. (1919).—b. 1874; asst. collr., E.A.P., 1897; employed on trans. duty during Uganda mutiny, 1898; collr., 1900; ag. Brit. vice-consul for G.E.A., Apr., 1900–Feb., 1901; sec. to the adminstn., 1903; Jubaland expedn., 1900–1, and Nandi expedn., 1905–6 (medal and two clasps); sec. for native affairs and M.L.C., 1907; on sp. serv. to Uga., Oct.–Nov., 1909; Swahili examiner, 1901–12; col. sec., S.L., 1913; ag. gov., periods, 1913–16; sec. to prov. admin., G.E.A. (1911). — Ed. at Corrig schl., Ireland, and St. Edward's, Oxford; 2nd lieut. 5th Royal Dublin Fus., Jan., 1887; capt., 1892; major, 1902; lieut.-col., 1906; B.S.A. Co. pol., and asst. comsnr., Rhodesia, 1890-92; certificates, R.I.C. and Dublin met. pol., 1895; asst. inspr., G. Coast Constaby. sources.text: LE MESSURIER, AUGUSTUS, C.I.E., Colonel, R.E., late Public Works Department, Government of India.—First commission, Bombay Engineers, Dec., 1856; served in the Indian Mutiny at the sieges of Forts Beyt and Dwarika; joined the Bombay public works department, as assistant engineer, May, 1860; was employed on the Karachi harbour works, on irrigation in Sind, on the Bombay harbour defences, &c.; executive engineer, March, 1863; deputy consulting engineer for railways, Bombay, Aug., 1864; served in the Abyssinian expedition, 1868 (medal); deputy consulting engineer for railways in Sind, Aug., 1871; acted as consulting engineer, Lahore, April-July, 1875; acted as secretary to the railway transport committee at Delhi, in 1875-76, and to a similar committee at Agra, 1876-77; deputed to Brussels exhibition to report on continental system of transport by railways, Aug., 1876; superintending engineer, May, 1877; officiating under secretary to government of India, railway branch, May, 1877, to Nov., 1878; served in the Afghan war, 1879-80, (medal and brevet of lieutenant-colonel); engineer-in-chief, Mysore state railway, Nov., 1879; joint secretary to chief commissioner, Mysore, 1880; on special duty reporting on timber-cutting operations in east of France, April, 1880; manager, Mysore state railway, Feb., 1881; consulting engineer to Mysore government, and secretary to chief commissioner, Coorg, March, 1882; superintending engineer, 1st class, Jan., 1883; engineer-in-chief, Bangalore-Harihar railway; 3rd chief engineer, March, 1887; on special duty, military department, Dec., 1887; officiating consulting engineer, railways, Calcutta, Feb., 1888; 2nd chief engineer, April, 1888; on special railway duty, Dec., 1888; chief engineer and secretary to government of Punjab, May, 1889; reverted to military duty, June, 1892. LE MÉSURIER, HAVILLAND, Indian C.S. (Bengal).—Educated at Rugby, and Balliol College, Oxford; appointed to the Bengal civil service after open competitive examination of 1884; arrived, 9th Nov., 1886; supernumerary assistant commissioner, Assam, Nov., 1886; assistant secretary and personal assistant to chief commissioner, March, 1891; transferred to Bengal as assistant magistrate and collector, April, 1892; joint magistrate and deputy collector, May, 1893. LE MÉSURIER, JOHN, Lieutenant-General, R.E., late Public Works Department, Bombay. —Joined Addiscombe, Feb., 1852; second lieutenant, Dec., 1853; arrived in India, 26th Nov., 1855; served in the public works department in Sind from June, 1856, as assistant engineer and executive engineer, and was employed on the Nara works and the Rohri canal, Hyderabad; served with the Persian expedition, 1856-57 (medal and clasp); on special duty, Karachi, Jan., 1867; acting superintending engineer for irrigation in Sind, April, 1871, to Dec., 1873, and for various periods between 1875 and 1880; superintendent of works, Western Indus, Karachi, Dec., 1873; superintending engineer, Jan., 1879; officiating chief engineer for irrigation and under secretary to government of Bombay, June-Aug., 1883; (temporary) chief engineer, 3rd class, and chief engineer for irrigation, and joint secretary to government, public works department (irrigation), March, 1884; superintending engineer in Sind, Jan., 1886; retired, March, 1887.

sources.text: MACDOUGALL, THE HON. WILLIAM, C.B. (1867).—Ed. at Victoria Univ., Cobourg; admitted an atty., Upper Canada, 1847; called to the bar, Hilary, 1862; founded (1848) the "Canada Farmer," subsequently merged in the "Canadian Agriculturist," which he published and edited until 1858; founded (1850) the "North American," a Reform newspaper, of which he was chief editor until merged in the Toronto "Daily Globe" in 1857; leading political writer on the "Daily Globe," from 1857 to 1860; represented Canada at the New York Exhibn., 1853; sec. of the Constitutional Reform Assoc. of Upper Canada, 1859; mem. of the exec. coun. and comsnr. of crown lands, Canada, May, 1862, to Mar., 1864; prov. sec. from June, 1864, and ag. min. of marine from July, 1866, until the union of the provinces, 1867; sworn of the Queen's privy coun. in Canada; min. of pub. wks. for the Dominion from July, 1867; lieut.-gov. of Rupert's Land and the N.W. territories, Oct., 1869; chmn. of the comsn. to open trade relations with the W. Indies, Mexico, and Brazil, 1865-6; deleg. to the Charlottetown Union confce., 1864; to that at Quebec in the same year; and to the col. confce. in London to complete terms of union of B.N.A. cols., 1866-7; deleg. to England, with late Sir G. E. Cartier, to confer with imperial authorities on the defences of the Dominion, and for the acquisition of the N.W. territory, 1868; comsnr. for Ontario, for the settlement of N.-W. boundary of the prov., 1871; sent to England by Dominion govt., 1873, as special comsnr. to confer with imperial govt. on subject of fisheries; returned to Canadian legislature in 1858, where he sat until the union of 1867, when returned to house of commons; elected to Ontario assem. in May, 1875; resig. Sept., 1878, and again returned to house of commons; ret. from public life, 1882, and resumed practice of his profession in Ottawa. Is a K.C.

(medal and clasp), the Bhutan campaign, 1865 (clasp), the Abyssinian expdn., 1868 (medal), and the Hazara campaign, 1868 (clasp); on special duty in Baluchistan, with Major R. Sandeman, 1875-77; asst. to govr.-gen.'s agent, Baluchistan, 1877; served in the Afghan campaign, 1878-80 (medal); C.S.I., Feb., 1881; asst. to the rest. in Mysore, and sec. to chief commr., Coorg, 1882; pol. agent, Bhopawar, Feb., 1885; Jhalawar, April, 1885; Bhopal, March, 1887; rest., Nepal, Oct., 1893; offg. agent to govr.-gen., Baluchistan, Feb., 1898; ret'd., April, 1900.

GABRIEL, SIR EDMUND VIVIAN, C.S.I., C.M.G., C.V.O., C.B.E., V.D., M.A., late Indian C.S.—Educ. at Emmanuel Coll., Cambridge; apptd. after exam. of 1897; arrived 7th Dec., 1898, and served in Bengal as asst. mag. and collr.; offd. as commr., Ajmer-Merwara, June-July, 1901; offd. as asst. to the agent to the govr.-gen. in Central India, Nov., 1901; asst. to pol. A.D.C. to S. of S., India Office, for H.M.'s coronation, June to July, 1902; on deputation as attache, govt. of India, Nov., 1902, to Jan., 1903; asst. sec. in the foreign dept., Feb., 1903; offg. under sec., March, 1905; confd., Nov., 1905; C.V.O., Jan., 1906; pol. offr. with the Prime Minister of Nepal, Sept., 1908; resdt. in W.R. States, Sept., 1908; sec. to chief commr., N.W.F. Prov., Jan., 1909; first asst. to agent to govr.-gen. in Central India, Oct., 1909; pol. agent and ditto, Feb., 1910; C.S.I., Dec., 1911; sec. to central cttee. for coronation Durbar, Delhi, Dec., 1910, to March, 1912; special duty, govt. of India for. dept., Jan., 1913, to March, 1914; on deputation to Bikaner State, March, 1914; on special duty under agent to the govr. gen. in the Rajputana, Sept., 1914; service, replaced with govt. of Bengal, March, 1915; on mil. duty, from March, 1915; finl. adviser, Occupied Enemy Territory, 1918-19; Knight of Justice of the Order of St. John of Jerusalem; Order of Crown of Italy (Officer); Order of St. Maurice and St. Lazarus (Officer); Italian War Cross; C.M.G., June, 1918; C.B.E., June, 1919; ret'd., Mar., 1920; knighted, May, 1937.

LATIFI, ALMA, C.I.E., O.B.E., M.A., LL.M. (Cantab.); LL.D. (Dublin), Barr. (1902), late, Indian C.S. (b. 12th Nov., 1879).—Educ. at Bombay (St. Xavier's Sch., and Coll.), Cambridge (St. John's Coll.), Paris and Heidelberg; apptd. after exam. of 1901; arrived, 8th Jan., 1903, and served in the Punjab as asst. commr., dist. judge, dep. commr., and commr.; on special duty to survey Punjab industries, 1909-10; serving under the govt. of India in connection with the press camps at the Coronation Durbar, Delhi, 1911-12; dir. of public instruction, Hyderabad state, Aug., 1913, to Aug., 1916; O.B.E., Dec., 1919; addl. secty. to govt., Punjab, Apl., 1921; sec. to govt. of Punjab, transf. depts., July, 1921 to Oct., 1924; member, Punjab leg. council, 1921-24; dep. commr., Karnal, 1924-27; commr., Ambala, Nov., 1927, and member, council of state, Nov., 1927 to Aug., 1928, and July, 1929 to Feb., 1930; member, Indian delegation to International law conference, Hague, Mar., 1930; substitute delegate and adviser, Indian delegation, International labour conference, Geneva, June, 1930; on duty with 1st, 2nd and 3rd round table conferences, London, Sept., 1930-Mar., 1931; Aug., 1931-Jan., 1932, and Oct., 1932-Jan., 1933 respectively, and with consultative ctee., I.R.T.C., Delhi, Jan. to Oct., 1932; commr., Multan, Mar., 1931; C.I.E., June, 1932; finl. commr. (rev.), Punjab, Mar., 1933, Feb., 1934, and again, Feb., 1936 to Jan., 1938; ret'd., Jan., 1938; author of "Effects of War on Property," and of "The Industrial Punjab."

(judge, high ct., Lahore) (b. 13th Dec., 1880).—Educ. at Owens Coll., Manchester; apptd. after exam. of 1903; arrived, 10th Dec., 1904, and served in the Punjab as asst. commr.; dist. and sess. judge, Nov., 1923; addl. judge, high ct., Lahore, March, 1927; actg. ditto, April, 1927; addl. ditto, from Nov., 1928; confd., Oct., 1933. SKINNER , ARTHUR FREDERICK, Office of High Commr. for India ( higher executive officer, store dept. (b. 28th May, 1887).—Apptd. 2nd class clerk, 22nd Sept., 1906; on mil. service from Dec., 1916, to Feb., 1919; transf. to office of high commr. for India, Oct., 1920; exec. officer, April, 1922; actg. higher exec. officer, June, 1929; confd., Nov., 1932. SKINNER , EDWARD LITTON, Indian Police ( dep. inspr.-genl. , Madras) (b. 25th Jan., 1885).—Joined the service as asst. supt., 19th Dec., 1904; supt., March, 1914; offg. dep. inspr.-genl., May, 1928; confd., Aug., 1930. SKINNER , JAMES MACGREGOR, M.B., Lt.-Col., I.M.S., rettd. (b. 14th Apl., 1880).—Joined the service, 1st Feb., 1906; surg., 1st Dist., Madras, and supt., Rayapuram medl. school, Feb., 1927; offg. 2nd physician, gen. hosp., Madras, Feb., 1926; confd., June, 1929; rettd., Apl., 1935. SKINNER , PHILIP ERNEST FREEMAN, Indian C.S. ( asst. commr., Central Provs. ) (b. 6th March, 1904).—Educ. at Charterhouse, and King's Coll., Cambridge; joined the service, 10th Oct., 1927; arrived, 12th Dec., 1927, and served in the Central Provs. as asst. commr.; under secty. to govt., C.P., Oct., 1931; offg. dep. commr., May, 1933. SKRINE , CLARMONT PERCIVAL, O.B.E., B.A., Indian C.S. (b. 28th Feb., 1888).—Educ. at Winchester, New College, Oxford, and Univ. Coll., London; apptd. after exam. of 1911; arrived, 25th Nov., 1912, and served in the United Provs. as asst. mag. and collr.; temp. asst. pol. agent and asst. commr., Sibi, Oct., 1915; H.B.M.'s vice-consul at Kerman, Oct., 1916; H.B.M.'s consul for Kerman and Persian Baluchistan, Dec., 1917; prob., pol. dept., Jan., 1918; under-sec. to govt. of India, for. and pol. dept., Jan., 1920; pol. agent, Quetta, April, 1921; H.M.'s consul-general, Kashgar, July, 1922; sec. to agent to govr.- gen., Punjab States, July, 1926; H.B.M.'s Consul for Sistan and Kain, April, 1927; pol. agent and dep. commr., Sibi, Mar., 1929; pol. agent, Kalat, Mar., 1932; and again, Dec., 1934; rev. and judl. commr. in Baluchistan, Aug., 1934; O.B.E., Nov., 1935. SLACKE , FRANCIS ALEXANDER, C.S.I., B.A., late Indian C.S.—Educ. at Taunton Coll. Sch., Univ. Coll., Oxford, and St. John's Coll., Cambridge; apptd. after exam. of 1874; arrived, 8th Dec., 1876, and served in Behgal as asst. mag. and collr.; settl. officer of wards and attached estates in Chota Nagpur; joint mag. and dep. collr., Jan., 1888; offd. as commr., Chittagong, Sept., 1890; mag. and collr., May, 1892; sec. to board of rev., Nov., 1896; sec. to govt. of Bengal, genl. depts., June, 1900; temp. commr., Feb., 1903; confd., Oct., 1903; offg. member, board of rev., Oct., 1905; offg. lieut.-govr. of Bengal, Aug. to Oct., 1906; member, board of rev., L.P., Land Rev. Dept., Aug., 1906; addl. member of govr.-gen.'s legisl. council, 1906, to March, 1908, and from Dec., 1908; presdt., board of examiners, Calcutta, Nov., 1908; member of lieut.-govr.'s exec. council, Nov., 1910; rettd., April, 1912; C.S.I., Jan., 1908. SLADE , MEAD, Indian C.S. ( collr. of customs, Bombay ) (b. 24th Jan., 1894).—Educ. at Ilminster Sch., and University Coll., London; on mil. service from Sept., 1914, to Oct., 1923; joined the service, 29th Oct., 1923, and served in Burma as asst. commr.; and asst. to commr. of settlmt. and land records, May, 1925; offg. dep. commr., Feb., 1927; confd., July, 1932; asst. collr., customs, Calcutta, April, 1928; offg. collr., ditto, May, 1930; ditto, Rangoon, Nov., 1932; ditto, Bombay, Oct., 1934. SLADEN , FRANCIS FARQUHAR, C.I.E., B.A., late Indian C.S. ( United Provs. ).—Educ. at the Charterhouse, and Balliol Coll., Oxford; apptd. after exam. of 1898; arrived, 12th Dec., 1899, and served in the N.W. Prov. and Oudh as asst. mag. and collr., and asst. commr.; joint mag., Nov., 1908; dep. commr., Nov., 1914; mag. and collr., Nov., 1918; dep. commr., Nov., 1920; C.I.E., June, 1923; rettd., Feb. 1925. SLADEN , JOSEPH, B.A., late Indian C.S.—Educ. at Balliol Coll., Oxford; apptd. after exam. of 1885; arrived, 19th Nov., 1888, and served in Bombay as asst. collr. and mag.; and in Sind as asst. commr., and Sindhi translr.; acting collr. and mag., May, 1898; 1st asst., Nov., 1900; junr. collr., July, 1903; offg. sec. to govt., genl., &c., depts., Dec., 1903, to Dec., 1905; senr. collr., Aug., 1907; commr. and agent to govr. in Kathiawar, April, 1912; rettd., May, 1916; temp. empd. in India Office, jud. and public dept., from April, 1921, to May, 1923. SLADEN , JOSEPH MAURICE, Indian C.S. ( asst. collr. and magte., Bombay ) (b. 22nd Feb., 1896).—Educ. at Winchester and New Coll., Oxford; joined the service, 27th Oct., 1920; arrived, 2nd Dec., 1920, and served in Bombay as asst. collr.; offg. asst. pte. sec. to govr., May to Nov., 1922; offg. collr. and dist. magte., and pol. agent, March, 1925; asst. commr. in Sind and Sindhi translator to govt., March, 1928; jt. secty., Indian round table conf., London, 2nd Session, Sept.-Dec., 1931; minister, Khairpur state, May, 1932.

SIVASANKARA MENON, KUMAR PADMA, B.A., Indian C.S. ( pol. officer ) (b. 18th Oct., 1898).—Educ. at Madras Univ. and Christ Church Coll., Oxford; joined the service, 1st Nov., 1922; arrived, 13th Dec., 1922, and served in Madras as asst. collr. and mag.; under-sec. to resdt., Hyderabad, Feb., 1925; under-sec. to C.C. and A.G.G. in N.W.F.P., May, 1927; dist. judge, Peshawar, Apl., 1929; agent to the govt. of India in Ceylon, Oct., 1929; dist. and sess. judge, Peshawar, Aug., 1934.

sources.text: TUPPER, THE RIGHT HON. SIR C., BART. (creat. 1888), P.C. (1907), G.C.M.G. (1886), K.C.M.G. (1879), C.B. (1867), M.D., L.R.C.S., Edin. (1843).—Born 2nd July, 1821; is an M.A. and D.C.L. of Acadia Coll., Nova Scotia; is gov. of Dalhousie Coll., Halifax (apptd. by Act of Parlmt., 1862); pres. of the Canadian med. assoc. from its formation, 1867, until 1870; mem. of exec. coun., and prov. sec. N.S., 1857-1860; and from 1863 to June, 1867; prime min. of that prov. from 1864 until he ret. from office with his govt. on the Union Act coming into force, 1st July, 1867; deleg. to England on public business from N.S. govt., 1858 and 1865; from the Dominion govt., Mar., 1868; leader of the delegn. from N.S. to the union confce. at Charlottetown, 1864; to that in Quebec in same year, and to final col. confce. in London, to complete terms of union, 1866-7; holds patent of rank and precedence from Her Majesty Queen Victoria as an exec. coun., N.S.; sworn of the P.C., June, 1870, and pres. of that body until 1st July, 1872, when apptd. min. of inl. rev.; min. of customs, Feb., 1873; resig. office with Sir John Macdonald, 5th Nov., 1873; min. of pub. wks., Oct., 1878; min. of rlys. and canals, 1879; represented Cumberland in parlmt. for 29 years in N.S. Assem., from 1855 until confederation in 1867, and in the Commons from that year until he resig. his seat in the cabinet and was apptd. high comsnr. for Canada, in London, May 24th, 1884; acted as exec. comsnr. for Dominion at the Antwerp Exhibn., 1885, and the Col. and Inl. Exhibn., London, 1886; resumed office in Canadian ministry as finance min., 1887; one of H.M.'s plenipotentiaries at fisheries confce. at Washington, 1887; re-apptd. high comsnr., May, 1888; joint plenipo., with the Marquis of Dufferin and Sir J. A. Crowe, for negotiating a commercial arrangement between Canada and France, 1892; S. of S. for Canada, Jan., 1896; premier, Mar. to June, 1896; leader of opposition in H. of C., 1896-1900.

Was a member of the executive council, and provincial secretary, Nova Scotia, from 1857, to 1860; and from 1863 to 30th June, 1867; and prime minister of that province from 1864 until he retired from office with his government on the Union Act coming into force, 1st July, 1867; was a delegate to England on public business from Nova Scotia government 1858 and 1865; from the Dominion government, Mar., 1868; leader of the delegation from Nova Scotia to the union conference at Charlottetown, 1864; to that in Quebec in same year, and to final colonial conference in London to complete terms of union, 1866-7; holds patent of rank and precedence from Her Majesty as an executive councillor, Nova Scotia; created C.B. (civil) 1867, K.C.M.G., 1879, and G.C.M.G. (1881), author of "a Letter to the Rt. R.M., Bathhurst, and sub-collr., Port Alfred; 1875, C.C., R.M., and sub-collr. of customs, Barbrmr. and chrmn. harbour bd., Mossel Bay; 1878-9, on special service to Griqualand W. as ag. auditor and treas.-gen. and C.C., Kimberley; 1879, ag. C.C. and R.M., Albany; 1879-80, ag. C.C. and R.M., King William's Town; 1880, col. sec. of the Transvaal, mem. of exec. coun. and legis. assem.; 1881, Br. res. in Transvaal State, and sub-comsnr. for compensation claims; 1884, ret. on pension, office being abolished by convention of 1884; 1889, ch. of Crim. Investig. dept. and comsur. of pol., Kimberley and Barkly West, Cape.

HUDSON, GEORGE.—1853, temporary clerk in Commissariat, King William's Town, passed Civil Service examination, Cape Colony; 1854, clerk to R.M.; 1854, 2nd clerk, Customs, Port Elizabeth; 1857, 3rd examining officer, Customs, Port Elizabeth; 1858, second ditto; 1860, chief clerk, Customs, Port Elizabeth; 1870, chief commissioner, R.M., Bathurst, and sub collector, Port Alfred; 1875, C.C., R.M., and sub-collector of customs, harbour-master, and chairman, Harbour Board, Mossel Bay; 1878-9, on special service to Griqualand West, as acting auditor and treasurer-general and C.C., Kimberley; 1879, acting C.C. and R.M., Albany; 1879-80, acting C.C. and R.M., King William's Town; 1880, col. secretary of the Transvaal, member of Executive Council and Leg. Assembly; 1881, British resident in the Transvaal State, and sub-comm. for compensation claims; 1881, retired on pension, office being abolished by convention of 1881; 1889, chief of Criminal Investigation Department and comm. of Police, Kimberley and Barkly West, Cape.

KEALY, SIR EDWARD HERBERT, Kt., C.I.E., M.A., late Indian C.S. (b. 7th June, 1873).—Educ. at Felsted, and Univ. Coll., Oxford; apptd. after exam. of 1896; arrived, 9th Dec., 1897; and served in Bengal as asst. mag. and collr.; offg. asst. commr., Merwara, March, 1902; ditto, Ajmer, April, 1904; 1st asst. to govr.-genl's agent in Central India, Sept., 1904; asst. sec., foreign dept., govt. of India, Aug., 1905; on special duty in foreign dept., Dec., 1905; pol. asst., Jan., 1907; asst. commr., Ajmer, May, 1907; pol. agent, N.W.F. Prov., July, 1908; divl. and sess. judge, Feb., 1909; supt. , census operations, Rajputana and Ajmer-Merwara, from May, 1910; transfed. to Bihar, April, 1912; addl. divl. and sess. judge, Derajat, Oct., 1914; ditto, Peshawar, Feb., 1915; sec. to chief commr., N.-W. Frontier Prov., May, 1915; pol. agent in Baghelkhand, March, 1922; and resdt. at Gwalior, May, 1922; resdt. at Baroda, Aug., 1924; C.I.E., July, 1926; offg. agent to govt. gen. in C.I., March, 1927; ditto, in States of Western India, Oct., 1927; confd., April, 1928; Kt., June, 1932; ret'd., Dec., 1932.

LYTTON (EARL OF), RIGHT HON. EDWARD ROBERT BULWER-LYTTON, G.C.B., G.C.S.I. —Born Nov. 8, 1831; educated at Harrow, and afterwards at Bonn; entered the diplomatic service in 1849, and served as attaché successively at Washington, Florence, Paris, the Hague, St. Petersburg, and Constantinople; from Jan., 1859, to Jan., 1863, he was attached to the Vienna embassy, during which period he acted as consul-general at Belgrade (Feb.-March, 1860), and was employed on a special mission to prevent the renewal of hostilities between the Turks and Servians; 2nd secretary in the diplomatic service, Oct., 1862; secretary of legation at Copenhagen, Jan., 1863, at Athens, May, 1864, and at Lisbon, April, 1865; successfully concluded the negotiation of a commercial treaty with Austria; transferred to Madrid, Feb., 1868; secretary of embassy at Vienna, Oct., 1868, and at Paris, Oct., 1872; during the periods of his service at Copenhagen, Lisbon, Vienna, and Paris he acted on several occasions as chargé-d'affaires, and during the absence of the ambassador at Paris, was accredited there as minister plenipotentiary; ambassador at Lisbon, Nov., 1874; viceroy and governor-general of India, April 12, 1876, to April, 1880; during his tenure of office as governor-general he presided at the Delhi assembly, on the proclamation of Her Majesty the Queen as Empress of India, Jan. 1, 1877, and was the object of an attempt at assassination, Dec., 1879; G.C.B., Dec., 1877; created an earl, April, 1880; a royal commissioner for the London exhibition of 1886; was appointed ambassador extraordinary and plenipotentiary to the French Republic, Nov., 1887; his published literary works include: 'Clytemnestra, the Earl's Return, the Artist and other Poems,' 1855; 'The Wanderer: a Collection of Poems in Many Lands,' 1859; 'Lucile,' 1860; 'Tannhauser, or the Battle of the Bards' (written in collaboration with the Hon. Julian Fane), 1861; 'Serbski Pesme,' a collection of the national songs of Servia, 1861; 'The Ring of Amasis,' 1863; 'Poetical Works of Owen Meredith,' 1867; 'Chronicles and Characters,' 1868; 'Orval, or the Fool of Time,' 1869; 'Julian Fane, a Memoir,' 1871; 'Fables in Song,' 1874; and 'The Speeches of Edward, Lord Lytton, &c.,' 1874.

sources.text: MAKINDALE, SIR ARTHUR HENRY TEMPLE, K.C.S.I., late Indian C.S. (Madras).—Educ. at Cheltenham Coll.; apptd. after exam. of 1873; arrived, 10th Nov., 1875; served in Madras as asst. collr. and mag., and in the foreign dept. of the govt. of India as attaché, and asst. and junr. under sec. to govt.; offg. asst. to rest. in Mysore and sec. to the chief commr. of Coorg, Feb., 1885; offg. rest., May-June, 1885; first asst. and sec. for Berar to the rest., Hyderabad, Nov., 1886; pol. agent, Quetta and Pishin, April, 1887; 1st asst. to govr.-gen.'s agent, Central India, Oct., 1888; pol. agent, Bhopal, July, 1890, and Jhalawar, Jan., 1892; commr., Ajmer-Merwara, May, 1894; acting rest., W. states of Rajputana, June, 1895; agent to govr.-genl., Rajputana, and chief commr., Ajmer-Merwara, Mar., 1898; C.S.I., May, 1900; K.C.S.I., June, 1904; ret'd., Oct., 1905.

sources.text: PELLEY, SIR LEWIS, Lieut.-General, K.C.B., K.C.S.I., M.P., Indian Staff Corps.—First commission, Bombay infantry, 1840; posted to the 17th N.I.; served as assistant resident, Baroda, and prosecuted the Khutup enquiries before the commission under Sir James Outram in 1851; deputy collector in Scinde, Dec., 1853; and assistant commissioner for jaghirs, in Scinde, June, 1855; personal assistant to the commissioner, 1856; served in the Persian expedition as A.D.C. to General Jacob, and political secretary to Sir Jas. Outram (medal); brigade-major, Scinde frontier force, Dec., 1858; deputy magistrate, Kurrachee, June, 1859; secretary of legation, Persia, 1859; chargé-d'affaires, Persia, 1860; served on a special mission through Persia, Herat, Afghanistan, and Beloochistan, in 1860 and 1861; on special duty at Calcutta, with Lord Canning, 1861; on a mission to the Comoro Islands, 1861; political agent at Zanzibar, 1861-62; political resident in the Persian Gulf, with local rank of lieutenant-colonel in Persia, from 1862 to 1873, during which period he was employed on various missions and negotiations with Arab chiefs in Arabia, and on the shores of the Persian Gulf, including a visit to the capital of the Wahabees, in 1865, and was associated with Sir Bartle Frere on an anti-slavery mission to the east coast of Africa and Arabia, in 1872 and 1873; agent to the governor-general, and chief commissioner, Rajputana, 1873 to 1878, and was deputed as special commissioner to Baroda in 1874, when he arrested the Guicowar, and took charge of the state; on special duty with the government of India in 1876; was appointed envoy extraordinary and plenipotentiary for Afghan affairs; K.C.S.I., June, 1874; K.C.B., Aug., 1877; has been a member of the council of the Royal Geographical Society, and of the Asiatic Society; author of a pamphlet on 'Our North-West Frontier,' 1858, 'Views and Opinions of General Jacob,' 'The Miracle Play of Hasan and Husein, collected from Oral Tradition,' 1879; was elected conservative member for North Hackney, Nov., 1885, and was re-elected in 1886.

PLOWDEN, TREVOR JOHN CHICHELE, C.S.I. , Indian C.S. — Educated at Winchester College; appointed to the Bengal civil service after open competitive examination of 1866; arrived in India, 31st Oct., 1868; assistant magistrate and collector in Bengal, Nov., 1868; on special duty in the Bengal secretariat, March, 1872, and Jan., 1873; officiating under secretary, government of Bengal, April, 1872; officiating under secretary, government of India, home department, Feb., 1873; inspector-general of police, Assam, Nov., 1876; on special duty as secretary to the prison conference, Jan., 1877; acted as under secretary, government of India, foreign department, from Jan., 1877, and was confirmed in that appointment, Dec., 1878; resident, 2nd class, and political agent, Turkish Arabia, March, 1880; consul-general, Baghdad, June, 1880; made a tour on Turco-Persian frontier, June–Sept., 1881; visited Karbala and Najaf, Nov., 1881, and Samara, Takrit, and the Upper Tigris, in April, 1885; commissioner of Ajmere-Merwara, June, 1885; resident in Meywar, Nov., 1885; officiating resident in Kashmir, April, 1886; confirmed, Nov., 1887; commissioner, Hyderabad assigned districts, Nov., 1888; officiating resident, Hyderabad, Nov., 1891; confirmed, March, 1892.

Dept., Govt. of India.—Joined the dept., 22nd May, 1890; asst. comptr., Burma, April, 1892; inspr. of local fund accts., Burma, Oct., 1893; asst. acctnt.-gen., Bombay, Dec., 1897; examr. of local fund accts., N.W. Prov. and Oudh, Jan., 1898; asst. acctnt.-gen., Burma, Dec., 1899; comptr., Assam, July, 1902; dep. acctnt.-gen., E. sources.text: SKRINE, SIR CLARMONT PERCIVAL, O.B.E., B.A., Indian C.S., Indian Political Service (b. 28th Feb., 1888).—Educ. at Winchester, New Coll., Oxford, and University Coll., London; apptd. after exam. of 1911; arrived, 25th Nov., 1912, and served in the United Provs. as asst. mag. and collr.; temp. asst. pol. agent and asst. commr., Sibi, Oct., 1915; H.B.M.'s vice-consul at Kerman, Oct., 1916; H.B.M.'s consul for Kerman and Persian Baluchistan, Dec., 1917; prob., pol. dept., Jan., 1918; under-sec. to govt. of India, for. and pol. dept., Jan., 1920; pol. agt., Quetta, Apl., 1921; H.M.'s consul-general, Kashgar, July, 1922; sec. to agent to govr.-gen., Punjab States, July, 1926; H.B.M.'s Consul for Sistan and Kain, Apl., 1927; pol. agt. and dep. commr., Sibi, March, 1929; pol. agt., Kalat, March, 1932; and again, Dec., 1934; rev. and judl. commr. in Baluchistan, Aug., 1934; O.B.E., Nov., 1935; offg. resdt., Madras States, Nov., 1936; confd. as 2nd class resdt., Nov., 1938; on depn., 1941; consul-gen., Khorasan, Oct., 1944; kt. Jan., 1946; addl. counsellor, Brit. Embassy, Tehran, Mar., 1946.

Abu, March, 1888; pol. agent and consul, Muscat, April, 1889; 1st asst. rest., Nov., 1889; transf. to Bushire, Dec., 1889; asst. pol. agent and consul, Bassora, April, 1890; 1st asst. agent, Baluchistan, April, 1891; pol. agent, S.E. Baluchistan, Oct., 1894; offg. pol. agent, Kotah, April, 1897; confd., June, 1899; first asst. to gov.-gen.'s agent, Central India, Nov., 1900; pol. agent, Eastern Rajputana States, Feb., 1901; ditto, Bikanir, Oct., 1904; resdt., W. Rajputana States, April, 1905; commr., Ajmer, Merwara, April, 1909; C.I.E., Dec., 1911; pol. offr., in charge of the ex-Amir Muhammad Yakub Khan of Kabul, and with Sardar Muhammad Ayub Khan, May, 1913; resdt. Jaipur, Nov., 1913; pol. offr. in charge of the ex-Amir Muhammad Yakub Khan, Dec., 1914; commdt., Imperial Cadet Corps, Feb., 1915; reverted to mil. duty, Aug., 1917; ret'd., Aug., 1919; author of a narrative of Muscat affairs, 1885-88.

Baluchistan, Oct., 1894; offg. pol. agent, Kotah, April, 1897; confd., June, 1899; first asst. to gov.-gen.'s agent, Central India, Nov., 1900; pol. agent, Eastern Rajputana States, Feb., 1901; ditto, Bikanir, Oct., 1904; resdt., W. Rajputana States, April, 1905; commr., Ajmer, Merwara, April, 1909; C.I.E., Dec., 1911; pol. offr., in charge of the ex-Amir Muhammad Yakub Khan of Kabul, and with Sardar Muhammad Ayub Khan, May, 1913; resdt. Jaipur, Nov., 1913; pol. offr. in charge of the ex-Amir Muhammad Yakub Khan, Dec., 1914; commdt., Imperial Cadet Corps, Feb., 1915; reverted to mily. duty, Aug., 1917; ret'd., Aug., 1919; author of a narrative of Muscat affairs, 1885-88.

sources.text: WINGATE, SIR ANDREW, K.C.I.E., late Indian C.S. (Bombay).—Educ. at Elizabeth Coll., Guernsey, Kensington Gr. Sch., Univ. of London, and Univ. of Heidelberg; apptd. after exam. of 1867; arrived, 8th Nov., 1869, and served in Bombay as asst. collr. and mag.; in pol. charge of the Jath state, 1876; addl. sec. in the famine dept., Mysore, Aug., 1877; asst. sec. to famine commn., Aug., 1878; C.I.E., June, 1879; settlt. officer in Udaipur state, Aug., 1879; offg. rest., Mewar, and settlt. officer, Kashmir state, Feb., 1887; junr. collr. and mag., Kanara, July, 1890; acting collr. of salt rev., Bombay, Oct., 1890; also acting commr. of customs, &c., April, 1891; settlt. officer, Udaipur state, 1891-93; senr. collr., Sept., 1893; addl. mem. of legisl. council, July, 1896, and again, Feb., 1898; offd. as commr. in Sind, Dec., 1896-June, 1897; K.C.I.E., Dec., 1898; sec. to govt., plague dept., and plague commr., April, 1900; commr., Aug., 1900; addl. member of legisl. council, Oct., 1900; ret'd., April, 1902.

sources.text: BELLAMY, CHAS. VINCENT, M.I.C.E., M.I.M.E., M.I.E.E., F.G.S., F.R.Met.Soc.—B. 1867; ed. Plymouth Coll.; Queen's Prizeman, S. Kensington, 1885; served articles under his father, Mr. G. D. Bellamy, M.I.C.E.; borough and water engnr., Plymouth, 1883 to 1886; asst. to Mr. J. C. Inglis, M.I.C.E., 1886; asst. to borough and water engnr., Plymouth, 1887; lieut., 2nd (P. of W.) V.B. Devon Regt., 1886 to 1889; lieut., Ceylon Light Infantry Vols. 1889 to 1895; capt., Southern Nigeria Volunteers, 1907; major, 1909; dist. engnr. P.W.D., Ceylon, May, 1889; 2nd financial asst., Colombo, 1889; dist. engnr., Pallai, Jan., 1890; dist. engnr., Vavoniya, Vilankulam, Apr., 1890; dist. engnr., Jaffna, Jan., 1891; exec. engnr., Victoria Bridge, Colombo, Sept., 1893; col. engnr. and survr.-gen., Dominica, W.I., Nov., 1895; also comsnr. ordnance property, July, 1897; nom. mem. Roseau Town Board, July, 1896; on special service at Antigua, Aug., 1896; and at Montserrat, Jan. and Feb., 1897; dir. pub. wks., Cyprus, May, 1898; also dir. of irrigtn., July, 1900; on spec. serv. in Egypt, Nov., 1902; dir. pub. wks. and dir. govt. telegraphs, Lagos, Jan., 1904; dir. pub. wks., S. Nigeria, on amalgamation with Lagos, 1st May, 1906; received thanks of S. of S., April, 1898, for a report on the pub. wks. of Dominica, and elaborated a scheme (since adopted) for the development of the island by means of roads; recd. thanks of govt., Jan., 1904, for services in Cyprus; hon. corres. sec. to Royal Col. Inst.; author of "Rainfall of Dominica"; "Climate of Cyprus"; "Rainfall in relation to Irrigation, Cyprus"; "Victoria Bridge, Colombo"; "Economic Construction of Roads"; "Monograph of the Main Roads of Cyprus"; "The Salt Lake of Larnaca, Cyprus"; compiled geological map of Cyprus, with key; joint author with Mr. A. J. Jukes Browne of "The Geology of Cyprus"; author of "A West African Smelting House," &c., &c.

DOWNING, CAPT. GEOFFREY GEORGE DAVID, J.P.—Ed. Corrig Schl., Ireland, Royal Irish Univ., and Royal Coll. of Surgeons, Ireland; served in Cape Mounted Rifles, 1883; Cape pol. (Griqualand West), 1888; Mashonaland exped. (Pioneers), 1890; Dominica defence res., 1904–1914; lieut., Nov., 1914; ag. sub-inspr., Leeward Is. pol., O.C., Montserrat defence force, O.C., local forces, Montserrat, Dec., 1916; ag. sub-inspr., Leeward Is. pol., and offr. instr., local forces, Antigua, July, 1917; O.C., Marine Batty., Antigua, Oct., 1917; O.C., flashlight service, Antigua-Montserrat, Jan., 1919; capt., Dominica defence force, 1919; O.C., Dominica defence force, Nov., 1919; manager, Barbuda and receiver of wrecks, Mar., 1920; mag., dist. L. (Barbuda), July, 1921. LL.D. (Aberdeen); F.R.S.; ed. Bedford schl.; lec. and demonstr. of chem. Oxford, 1884-86; prof. of chem., Pharm. Soc., 1886-96; lec. on chem., St. Thomas' Hosp., 1892-1900; sec., chem. soc., 1903-5; vice-pres., 1903-6; pres. section of chem. and agric. science, Brit. Assoc., 1906; mem. of coun., Royal Soc., 1904-7; mem. of advisory comtee. on trop. agric., C.O., 1908, vice-pres., Internat. assoc. of trop. agric., 1907; pres., 1910; pres., Internat. Congress trop. agric., London, 1914; mem. comml. intell. comtee. Bd. of T., 1900-6; dir., scientific and tech. dept., Impl. Inst., 1896-1903; dir., Impl. Inst., from 1903 to 1923; reported on agric. resources of Cyprus for C.O. in 1904, and of Asia Minor in 1907 (reports presented to parlmt.); visited Ceylon at request of colonial govt., 1910, and again in 1913; visited Newfoundland at request of colonial govt., 1914; arranged and supervised govt. min. surveys in Ceylon, N. and S. Nigeria and Nyassaland (reports presented to parlmt.); author of numerous scientific papers in the Phil. Trans. and Proceedings of Royal Soc., chem. soc., etc., and of tech. reports relating to the utilisation of the resources of the colonies, including "Cotton Cultivation in the Brit. Empire and in Egypt," 1904, "Brit. Cotton Cultivation," 1908; edited "Tech. Reports and Scientific Papers," Impl. Inst., 1903; "Selected Reports," Imp. Inst., 1909 (presented to Parlmt.); "Reports on work of Impl. Inst., 1906-14" (presented to Parlmt.); "Report on present position of Cotton Cultivation," 1910; editor, Imp. Inst. Handbooks on Commercial Resources of Tropics; author of article, "Rubber," in last edition "Ency. Brit."

GIDNEY, SIR CLAUDE HENRY, K.C.I.E., C.S.I., B.A., Indian C.S., ret'd., late Indian Political Service (b. 23rd Nov., 1887).—Educ. at Haileybury, Hertford Coll., Oxford, and University Coll., London; apptd. after exam. of 1911; arrived, 23rd Nov., 1912, and served in the United Provs. as asst. mag. and collr.; held various temp. appts. under govt. of India, for. and pol. dept., from Oct., 1914; pol. offr. (on probn.), and asst. pol. agent, Quetta, Jan., 1918; asst. for Mekran to pol. agent, Kalat, Sept., 1918; pol. agent, Sibi, Nov., 1919; second asst. to agent to govr.-genl. in Baluchistan, Feb., 1920; sec. to pol. resdt., Persian Gulf, Aprl., 1921; dep. commr., Bannu, Dec., 1923; ditto, Dera Ismail Khan, Nov., 1926; secty. to ch. commr. and agent to govr.-genl., N.W.F.P., May, 1928; dep. commr., Bannu, May, 1930; secty. to ch. commr. and agent to govr.-genl., N.W.F.P., Nov., 1930; ch. secty. to govt., N.W.F.P., June, 1932; mem., exec. council of govr., N.W.F.P., Aprl. and Nov., 1932; C.I.E., June, 1932; commr., Ajmer-Merwara, Nov., 1934; member, govr.'s exec. council, N.W.F.P., May, 1936; resdt., Hyderabad Aprl., 1937; C.S.I., May, 1937; resdt. at Hyderabad, Oct., 1938; confd. as resdt., cl. I, March, 1941; K.C.I.E., Jan., 1942; ret'd., 27th Sep., 1944.

sources.text: GOODFELLOW, GEORGE RISTO, Colonel, I.S.C., C.I.E., Political Department, Bombay.—First commission, Bombay infantry, Dec., 1854; arrived in India, Oct., 1854, and was employed on military duty till Jan., 1863, also serving as personal assistant to inspector-general of prisons, Poona, Oct., 1859, to March, 1860; from Jan., 1863, to April, 1870, served in the political department, at Aden, as Arabic interpreter to the resident, and as assistant resident, and acted for various periods as resident; acting special assistant political agent in charge of Rājkot and Gondal states, Kāthiāwar, April, 1870; from March, 1871, to Feb., 1872, served in Central India as officiating political agent, Baghelkhand; from May, 1872, served under the government of Bombay as acting political agent, Cutch, acting political superintendent, Akalkot, and assistant resident and acting resident at Aden; political agent, Mahi Kantha, Sept., 1880; political agent and collector of stamp revenue, Cutch, Sept., 1881; 2nd grade political agent, Feb., 1885; C.I.E., Aug., 1887; political superintendent, Palanpur, 1st grade, Feb., 1889.

Dept., Bombay.—Arrived, 13th Nov., 1859, and served under the mil. dept.; from Nov., 1863, served as asst. supt. of rev. survey and assessment, Gujarat; acting supt. of the Rajkot and Limbdi states, and acting asst. rest. at Aden, and at Baroda; asst. gen. supt. for thagi and dakaiti, Oct., 1871; asst. pol. agent, Mahi Kantha, July, 1872; from Oct., 1873, served as supt. of surveys under rajasthanik court, Kathiawar; acting joint administrator of Gondal state, 1880-81, and was on special duty with the Thakur Saheb in Europe, 1883; on special duty to inquire into administration of Rajpipla state, Nov., 1883; third asst. pol. agent, Kathiawar, Feb., 1885, continuing to be supt. of surveys; prest. of the rajasthanik court, Jan., 1886; pol. supt., Savantvadi, May-Oct., 1891; pol. agent, &c., Kolhapur; offd. in Kathiawar, Jan., 1894; and again from March, 1895; returned to Europe, May, 1896.

Goold-Adams, G.C.M.G.), and clk. of exec. coun., Oct., 1911; asst. sec. to govt., Cyprus, 1912; ag. comsnr., Paphos, 1917; comsnr., Famagusta, 1918; sec., Cyprus defence comtee., Aug., 1914; served in H.M.S. Doris on Syrian Coast 1914-1915; political offr. to Admirals Lord Wester Wemyss and Christian and govt. sec., Mudros, Feb., 1915 to June, 1916; (lieut.-comdr., and ag. comdr., R.N.V.R.); recd. thanks of admy.; Italian med. for mily. valour; political offr. to Admiral of the Fleet Sir J. de Robeck, Constantinople and Black Sea, Aug., 1919; Br. ch. comnr. in Georgia, Armenia and Azerbaijan, Apr. to Sept., 1920; asst. gov. of Jerusalem, Oct., 1920; mem. of comsns. on the Orthodox Patriarchate of Jerusalem, and on the Jaffa disturbances, 1921, and finan. comsnr. of the Patriarchate, 1921-24; col. sec., Sierra Leone, May, 1924; ch. sec., Palestine, July, 1928; accredited rep. to Perm. Mandates Comsn., 1930; lieut. gov., Malta, Aug., 1930; gov. and commdr.-in-ch., Fiji, and high comsnr. for W. Pac., 1938; passed in Turkish and modern Greek (hons.); author of "A Bibliography of Sierra Leone." 1910 and 1925; "Cyprus under the Turks," 1921; "An Eastern Chequerboard," 1934; "More Moves on an Eastern Chequerboard," 1935; "The Making of Modern Turkey," 1936; joint editor, "Handbook of Cyprus," and "Handbook of Palestine and Transjordan".

NORTON.—Called to the bar, Lincoln's Inn, Trinity, 1888; clerk in census office, Mauritius, Feb., 1871; clerk in the procureur and advocate general's office, Aug., 1871; acted on several occasions as secretary to the prison committee of Port Louis; district cashier of Port Louis June, 1878; assistant clerk to the district and stipendiary courts of Black River, Feb., 1874; secretary to the special commissioner to inquire into the condition of labourers in the dependencies of Mauritius, June, 1874; joint district clerk, Black River, Sept., 1876; joint district clerk, Plaines Wilhems district, Oct., 1877; deputy registrar of the Supreme Court of Penang, April, 1880; is author of an index to the laws of the Straits Settlements; acting second magistrate and commissioner, court of requests, Singapore, and J.P. for the Straits Settlements, Jan., 1884; passed in Malay, April, 1884; acting registrar, commissioner of the Court of Requests, and collector of stamps, Malacca, Aug., 1885; has edited the cases decided in the supreme court, Straits Settlements, 1880-4.

KYSHE, J. W. NORTON.—Passed the civil service examination in 1871; appointed to the census office, Mauritius, 21st February, 1871; clerk in the procureur and advocate general's office, 3rd August, 1871; acted on several occasions as secretary to the prison committee of Port Louis; district cashier of Port Louis, June, 1873; first assistant clerk to the district and stipendiary courts of Black River, 14th February, 1874; secretary to the special commissioner appointed to inquire into the condition of labourers in the dependencies of Mauritius, 12th June, 1874; acting cashier of Grand Port, 15th May, 1875; joint district clerk, and assistant officer of the civil status, Black River, 20th September, 1876; commissioned to pass engagements and effect discharges of labourers in lieu of the stipendiary magistrate of Black River, 1st Feb., 1877; joint district clerk, and assistant officer of the civil status of Plaines Wilhems district, 23rd October, 1877; deputy registrar of the Supreme Court of Penang, 17th April, 1880; is a commissioner of oaths, &c.; acted as registrar from 1st May to 23rd Sept., 1881, and also as registrar of the vice-admiralty court during the same period; again acted as registrar and as registrar of joint stock companies and of the vice-admiralty court, from 12th April to 31st December, 1882, and also from 1st January, 1883 to 28th September, 1883; and a fourth time from 2nd October to 9th November, 1883; is author of an index to the laws of the Straits Settlements; acting second magistrate and commissioner, court of requests, Singapore, and J.P. for the Straits Settlements, 31st Jan., 1884; acting senior magistrate, 11th June to 17th Aug., 1884; passed in Malay, 15th April, 1884; acting registrar, with special judicial duties in the absence of a judge, commissioner of the Court of Requests, and collector of stamps, Malacca, 25th August, 1885.

sources.text: LE MESSURIER, AUGUSTUS, C.I.E., Col., R.E., late India Public Works Dept.—First commn., Bombay engrs., Dec., 1856; served in the Mutiny; joined the Bombay public works dept., May, 1860; exec. engr., March, 1863; dep. consulting engr. for railways, Bombay, Aug., 1864; served in the Abyssinian expedn., 1868 (medal); dep. consulting engr. for railways in Sind, Aug., 1871; sec. to the railway transport committees, 1875-76 and 1876-77; suptg. engr., May, 1877; offg. under sec. to govt. of India, railway branch, 1877-78; served in the Afghan war, 1879-80 (medal); engr.-in-chief, Mysore state railway, Nov., 1879; joint sec. to chief commr., Mysore, 1880; manager, Mysore state railway, Feb., 1881; consulting engr. to Mysore govt., and sec. to chief commr., Coorg, March, 1882; engr.-in-chief, Bangalore-Harihar railway; offg. consulting engr., railways, Calcutta, Feb., 1888; chief engr. and sec. to govt. of Punjab, May, 1889; reverted to mil. duty, June, 1892; ret'd. from the army, May, 1893.

sources.text: LOFTUS, THE RIGHT HON. SIR AUGUSTUS WILLIAM FREDERICK SPENCER, commonly called Lord Augustus Loftus, K.C.B. (1862), G.C.B. (1866), privy councillor (1868). — Attaché at Berlin, 1837; paid attaché at Stuttgart, July, 1844; served with the special missions in Berlin and Vienna, 1848; secretary of legation at Stuttgart, Jan., 1852, transferred to Berlin, May, 1853; chargé d'affaires there in portions of 1853, 1855, and 1857; envoy at Vienna, March, 1858, at Berlin, Dec. 1860, and at Munich, 1862; ambassador at Berlin, 1865; was accredited to the North German Confederation from 1868 to Oct., 1871, when he was made ambassador at St. Petersburg until early in 1879, when he was appointed governor of New South Wales; resigned 1885.

LOGAN, ROBERT, Bengal C.S. —Educated at the Royal Academy, Inverness, and University College, London; matriculated at the London University; appointed to the Bengal civil service after open competitive examination of 1867; arrived in India, 28th Oct., 1869; served in the Central Provinces from 1869 to 1881, in the grade of assistant commissioner, and officiated as district superintendent of police, March, 1872; inspector of schools, Dec., 1873, to March, 1874, and registrar of the judicial commissioner's court, April, 1874, to Dec., 1876; from April to Nov., 1881, served in the financial department in Bengal as officiating deputy accountant-general and officiating accountant-general; appointed assistant comptroller-general in Class III of the financial department, Sept., 1881; acted as under secretary, government of India, finance and commerce department, from Nov., 1881, and was confirmed in this appointment, July, 1883; officiated as accountant-general, N.W. Provinces and Oudh, and deputy commissioner of paper currency, Aug.-Oct., 1883, and as deputy accountant-general, Feb., 1884; officiating accountant-general, Bengal, March, 1884; deputy accountant-general, Bengal, Sept., 1884; officiating accountant-general, Punjab, March, 1885.

McDONALD, O. J.—B. 1859; Out Island comsr. (4th div.), Bahamas, 1909. couns., Jan., 1877; has acted as registr.-gen., agt.-gen. of immigr., and comsnr. of lands; engaged, 1876, in the suppression of the disturbances in the mountains of Viti Levu, for which he was voted a gratuity of 200l.; joint comsnr., 1877, for the settlement of debts due from natives and Europeans, and for the settlement of all pecuniary claims against the late govt. of Fiji; mem. of the Native Regulation Board, 1877; proceeded to Tonga, 1879, to report on the financial condition of that country; ag. col. sec., Nov., 1883, to June, 1884, and Oct., 1874, to Jan., 1875; admstr. of the govt., and ag. high comsnr. and consul-gen. for the W. Pacific, Jan. to Aug., 1875; representative of Fiji at the first session of the Fed. Coun. of Australasia, at Hobart, Jan., 1885; Albert medal of the 2nd class (1884), with the Clarke gold medal of the Roy. Hum. Soc. of Australasia in 1885, for saving life at sea; dep. admstr. of Fiji, Sept., 1885, and Aug., 1886; declared the Queen's sovereignty over Br. New Guinea, Sept., 1888; admstr., Br. New Guinea, 1888; lieut.-gov., 1895; gov. Lagos, 1899; represented the W. African colonies and protectorates at Coronation, 1902; gov., Newfoundland, 23rd July, 1904; gov., Queensland, 6th May, 1909.

sources.text: MEADE, SIR RICHARD JOHN, General, K.C.S.I., C.I.E., Indian Staff Corps.—Educated at Royal Naval School; appointed a cadet, Bengal Infantry, 1st March, 1838; arrived in India, July, 1838; served with the 65th and 54th regiments, N.I., and also temporarily in the commissariat department; interpreter and quartermaster, 65th regiment, N.I., Jan., 1844; station staff at Nowgong, Oct., 1845; 2nd in command, 6th infantry, Gwalior contingent, Dec., 1845; brigade major, Gwalior contingent, postmaster, Gwalior, and cantonment magistrate, Morar, Nov., 1851; also paymaster and commissariat officer, May, 1853; served with 65th Regiment, N.I., in Burma, 1853-55, and was appointed assistant adjutant-general, Pegu division, Oct., 1854; on the mutiny of the Gwalior contingent, escaped to Agra, where he raised a body of cavalry, subsequently known as 'Meade's Horse'; in June, 1858, escorted Maharaja Sindhia back to Gwalior, and was present at the battle at that place, Sindhia's palace being surrendered to him personally; was afterwards employed as special commissioner in Gwalior to deal with the Gwalior State troops; in 1859 joined brigadier-general Sir R. Napier's force, and received the surrender of Raja Man Sing, and captured the rebel leader, Tantia Topee; in July, 1859, surprised and routed a large body of rebels at Gurroya in the Jhansi district; brevet-major, mutiny medal and clasp for Central India; political agent, Gwalior, April, 1860; governor-general's agent in Central India, and opium agent, Malwa, Nov., 1861; chief commissioner of Mysore and Coorg, Feb., 1870; president of special commission to inquire into charges against the Gaekwar of Baroda, Oct., 1873; member of the commission to investigate the charge preferred against the Gaekwar of attempting to poison the resident, Colonel R. Phayre, C.B., Feb., 1875; appointed to the charge of the Baroda state as agent and special commissioner, April, 1875, and superintended the measures necessary for the re-organisation of the administration, and the selection of a successor to the deposed Gaekwar; resident at Hyderabad, Dec., 1875, to March, 1881; C.S.I., June, 1866; K.C.S.I., May, 1874; C.I.E., Jan., 1878; lieutenant-general in the army, Sept., 1884; general, Jan., 1889.

(1892).—B. 1840; asst. clk., imigrn. dept., Trinidad, 1858; warden of the dist. of Montserrat, and comsnr. of crown lands, 1867; sub-intendant of crown lands, 1869; was a J.P., mem. of the cent. road bd., and of the bd. of health; asst. protector of imigrts., Mauritius, 1872; received the thanks of H.M.'s roy. comsnrs. for special services rendered during their inquiry into the treatment of Indian imigrts. in that col.; acted as agt.-gen. of imigrn. in Trinidad in 1873; govt. imigrn. agt. in India, Oct., 1873; ag. emigrn. agt. for Jamaica, 1876; agt.-gen. for imigrn., Br. Guiana, 1881; emigrn. agt. for Br. Guiana, in Calcutta, 1884; in 1885 modified emigrn. rules under Act of 1883, and in 1886 obtained extension of Indian P.O. money order system to Br. Guiana and other W. Ind. cols.

sources.text: PEILE, SIR JAMES BRAINTWAITE, K.C.S.I., M.A. , late Bombay C.S., and late member of the Council of India.—Educ. at Oriel Coll., Oxford; apptd. to the Bombay civil service after exam. of 1855; arrived 8th Oct., 1856, and served in Bombay as asst. collr. and mag.; on special duty for inquiry into claims of thakurs of Bhaunagar on account of land and sea customs, May, 1859; specially apptd. to inquire into condition of talukdars, Ahmadabad, Jan., 1860; alienation settl. officer, Gujarat, April, 1861; asst. to rev. commr., Dec., 1861; under sec. to govt. of Bombay, rev. dept., April, 1862; on special duty for carrying out provisions of bill for relief of the talukdars, Ahmadabad, Dec., 1862; commr. for revising subord. civil establs., April, 1866; registrar-gen. of assurances, July, 1866; dir. of public instrn., April, 1869; acting municipal commr. Bombay, May—Oct., 1872; acting pol. agent, Kathiawar, Jan., 1873; on duty at Delhi in connection with imperial assemblage, Dec., 1876; acting commr. in Sind, June, 1878; member of famine commn., 1878-79; acting sec. to govt., pol., &c., depts., March, 1879; from April, 1879, served as sec. in the rev., finl., and gen. depts., and acted as chief sec.; on special duty on famine commn. in England, 1879-80; on special duty in India, 1880 and 1881; member of council, Bombay, Dec., 1882; acted as govr. and prest. in council in March, 1885; temporary member of govr.-gen.'s council, Oct., 1886; ret'd., Nov., 1887; member of council of India, 12th Nov., 1887; vice-prest., 1894-95; K.C.S.I., Jan., 1888; member of royal commn. on Indian expenditure, May, 1895; ret'd. from Council of India, Nov., 1902.

PEILE, SIR JAMES BRAINTWAITE, M.A., K.C.S.I., late Bombay C.S.—Educated at Oriel College, Oxford; appointed to the Bombay civil service after open competitive examination of 1855; arrived in India, 8th Oct., 1856, and served as assistant collector and magistrate; on special duty, alienation department, Nov., 1858; on special duty for inquiry into claims of thakurs of Bhavnagar on account of land and sea customs, May, 1859; especially appointed to inquire into condition of talukdars, Ahmedabad, Jan., 1860; alienation settlement officer, Gujerat, April, 1861; assistant to revenue commissioner, Dec., 1861; under secretary to government of Bombay, revenue department, April, 1862; on special duty for carrying out provisions of bill for relief of the talukdars, Ahmedabad, Dec., 1862; commissioner for revising subordinate civil establishments, April, 1866; registrar-general of assurances, July, 1866; director of public instruction, April, 1869; acting municipal commissioner, Bombay, May-Oct., 1872; acting political agent, Kathiawar, Jan., 1873; on duty at Delhi in connection with Imperial assemblage, Dec., 1876; acting commissioner in Sind, June, 1878; on special duty as member of famine commission, Aug., 1878, to March, 1879; acting secretary to government, political, secret, judicial, and educational departments, March, 1879; from April, 1879, served as secretary in the revenue, financial, and general departments, and acted as chief secretary; on special duty on famine commission in England, Oct., 1879, to July, 1880; on special duty in India, Nov.-Dec., 1880, and in June, 1881; member of council, Bombay, Dec., 1882; acted as governor and president in council in March, 1885; temporary member of governor-general's council, Oct., 1886; retired, Nov., 1887; member of council of India, 12th Nov., 1887; vice-president, 1894-95; K.C.S.I., Jan., 1888.

PHILIPPO, SIR GEORGE, KNT.—Admitted to the honourable society of the Inner Temple, April, 1859; obtained a certificate of honour of the first class, Jan., 1862; called to the bar, Hilary term, 1862; admitted to the Jamaica bar, June, 1862; practised at the Jamaica bar until Feb., 1868; appointed queen's advocate, Sierra Leone, March, 1868, and acting judge of the court of summary jurisdiction during the absence on leave of Mr. Justice Huggins, August, 1868; attorney-general of British Columbia, March, 1870; appointed on a commission to collect, revise, and publish a complete edition of the laws of that colony, 1871; nominated a non-elective member of the legislative council under the new constitution, Dec. 1870; prepared, under the direction of the government, "The Constitution Act, 1871," and the several other measures necessary to enable British Columbia to enter into confederation with Canada, puisne judge of the supreme court of British Guiana, May, 1871; went to Gibraltar on special service, Sept., 1873; acting attorney-general and judge of the court of requests, Gibraltar; on special service in Gibraltar, Dec., 1873, to Feb., 1874; junior puisne judge, Straits Settlements, Dec., 1873; and senior puisne judge, March, 1874; attorney-general, Hong Kong, August, 1876; chief justice and judge of the court of requests, Gibraltar, Aug., 1879; chief justice of Hong Kong, 1881.

PHILLIPPO, GEORGE.—Admitted to the honourable society of the Inner Temple, April, 1859; obtained a certificate of honour of the first class, Jan., 1862; called to the bar, Hilary term, 1862; admitted to the Jamaica bar, June, 1862; practised at the Jamaica bar until Feb., 1868; during that time was professionally engaged before the royal and special commissioners appointed in consequence of the serious disturbances in that island, and of the measures of repression taken by the Government; was detained in England for some months by the Jamaica committee in order to give evidence as to the laws of Jamaica in the various prosecutions instituted by that body; appointed queen's advocate, Sierra Leone, March, 1868, and acting judge of the court of summary jurisdiction during the absence on leave of Mr. Justice Huggins, August, 1868; attorney-general of British Columbia, March, 1870; appointed on a commission to collect, revise, and publish a complete edition of the laws of that colony, 1871; prepared the proclamation necessary for bringing the new constitution of that colony into operation under the order in council, 1870, whereby representative institutions were to some extent conceded; nominated a non-elective member of the legislative council under the new constitution, Dec., 1870; prepared the address from the legislature of British Columbia to Her Majesty for union with Canada, and prepared and passed through the legislative council, under the direction of the government, "The Constitution Act, 1871," and the several other measures necessary to enable British Columbia to enter into confederation with Canada, with full representative institutions and under "responsible government;" puisne judge of the supreme court of British Guiana, May, 1871; went to Gibraltar on special service, Sept., 1873; acting attorney-general and judge of the court of requests, Gibraltar; on special service in Gibraltar, Dec., 1873, to Feb., 1874; junior puisne judge, Straits Settlements, Dec., 1873; and senior puisne judge, March, 1874; attorney-general, Hong Kong, August, 1876; chief justice and judge of the court of requests, Gibraltar, Aug., 1879.

SADASHIVA RAU, KALLE RAMA RAU, B.A. , late Indian Finance Dept. (b. 16th July, 1884.)—Joined the service, 3rd March, 1908; asst. acctnt.-gen., Madras, Nov., 1909; ditto, United Provs., Nov., 1915; dep. acctnt.-gen., Bengal, Jan., 1919; ditto, Madras, March, 1919; ditto, Bombay, Sept., 1924; ditto, Central Provs., April, 1925; offg. dep. dir., army audit, Jan., 1927; offg. acct.-genl., Central Provs., Mar., 1930; ch. auditor, E.B. SADASIVA AIYAR , Sir THEAGARAJA AIYAR , Kt., B.A., M.L., Diwan Bahadur.—Joined the provincial civil service, Madras, 17th March, 1887, and served as dist. munsif; sub. judge, Jan., 1905; dist. and sess. judge, Sept., 1910; addl. judge, Madras high ct., Feb., 1912, to Feb., 1914; judge, Feb., 1914; knighted, June, 1921; retd., June, 1921. SADASIVAM , TUMULURU RAMAKRISHNIAH , B.A., Finance dept., govt. of India ( dep. acct. genl., Bombay ) (b. 27th Nov., 1892).—Joined the service as probnr., 9th Feb., 1915; asst. contr., paper currency, Nov., 1916; asst. acct. genl., posts and tels., Madras, 24th June, 1921; asst. acct.-genl., C.P., Oct., 1921; asst. acct.-genl., posts and tels., Calcutta, Mar., 1922; dep. ditto, Oct., 1924; asst. dir. of army audit, W.C., Mar., 1926; ditto, S.C., May, 1927; audit officer, N.W.F.P., Feb., 1930; asst. acct.-genl., posts and tels., Delhi, Jan., 1931; dep. ditto, Jan., 1931; dep. acct.-genl., Bombay, Apr., 1931. SADHU , RAJENDRA LAL , M.A., B.L., late Bengal Civil Service.—Apptd. sub-judge, April, 1919; addl. dist. and sess. judge, Jan., 1923; retd., Jan., 1927. SADHU RAM , CHAUDHRI , B.A., Indian Police Service (b. 24th July, 1899).—Joined the service as asst. supt., Punjab , 6th Oct., 1922; offg. supt., Feb., 1928. SADHU , TARAK NATH , Rai Bahadur, C.I.E., Judl. Dept., Bengal (b. Oct., 1875).—Joined the service as public prosecutor, presdy. mag.'s ct., Calcutta , 12th May, 1920; C.I.E., June, 1924. SADIK , HAMID GHULAM ( see Hamid G. S.). SADULLAH KHAN , KHAN BAHADUR , Indian Political Dept. ( pol. officer ) (b. 29th Decr., 1880).—Joined the dept. as asst. commr., Peshawar, on 1st Jan., 1922; city magte., Peshawar, Apr., 1929; dist. judge, Hazara, May, 1930; asst. pol. agent in Southern States of C.I. and in Malwa, June, 1931. SAGREIYA , KAMPTA PRASAD , B.A. (Oxon), B.Sc., Indian Forest Service (b. 10th Feb., 1904).—Joined the service as asst. conserv., Central Provs. , 27th Oct., 1927. SAH , DEBI LAL ( see Debi Lal Sah). SAHAI , RAM CHANDRA ( see Ram Chandra Sahai). SAHAI , RAMESHWAR ( see Rameshwar Sahai). SAHASRABUDHE , DATTATRAYA LAKSHMAN , M.Ag., M.Sc., Rai Bahadur, Indian Agric. Service ( agric. chemist to govt. of Bombay ) (b. 1st Sept., 1881).—Held non-gazetted appts. from 3rd Jan., 1906, to 31st May, 1913; asst. prof. of chemistry, June, 1913; agric. chemist, March, 1926. SAHAY , BHAGWAN , Indian C.S. ( asst. mag. and coll., United Provinces ) (b. 15th Feb., 1905).—Educ. at University of Allahabad and School of Oriental Studies, London; joined the service, 9th Oct., 1929; arrived, 10th Nov., 1929, and served in the United Provinces as asst. mag. and coll. SAHAY , JAYADEVA , M.A., Indian Police Service (b. 2nd Jan., 1900).—Joined the service as asst. supt., Bihar and Orissa , 30th April, 1923. SAHAY , KULWANT , Judl. Dept., Bihar and Orissa ( judge, high ct., Patna ) (b. 23rd Jan., 1873).—Apptd. addl. judge, high ct., Patna Nov., 1923; judge, ditto, Dec., 1927. SAHAY , VISHNU , B.Sc., Indian C.S. ( Jt. mag., United Provs. ) (b. 22nd Nov., 1901).—Educ. at Allahabad Univ., and Lincoln Coll., Oxford; joined the service, 23rd Oct., 1925; arrived, 7th Dec., 1925, and served in the United Provs. as asst. mag.; dep. commr. Apr., 1928. SAHIB , ABDUR RAHIM ( see Abdur Rahim Sahib). SAHIB , ELATT VILIAGATH AMU ( see Amu Sahib, E. V.). SAHIB , MUHAMMAD SIRAJUDDIN ( see Muhammad S.S.). SAHIB , SAYID ABDUL QADIR ( see Saiyid Abdul Qadir S.). SAHIB , SHARIF MUHAMMAD ALI ( see Sharif M. A. S.). SAHIBZADA , AHMED KHAN , M.B., Major, I.M.S. ( agency surg. ) (b. 15th Oct., 1891).—First commn. dated 1st March, 1922; in milty. employ to April, 1925; civil medl. officer, Bannu, April, 1925; ditto, Tochi Agency, April, 1928; ditto, N. Waziristan, Nov., 1929. SAHNEY , NAUBAT RAI , LALA, B.A., LL.B., Indian Police Service (b. 29th June, 1901).—Joined the service as asst. supt., Punjab , 7th July, 1924; offg. supt., Sept., 1929. SAHNI , NARSING DASS M. , B.A., B.Sc., Indian Forest Service (b. 12th Oct., 1900).—Joined the service as asst. conserv., Madras , 9th Nov., 1923. SAID , MUHAMMAD ( see Muhammad Said). SAID ULLAH KHAN , B.A. (Oxon), Barr. Indian C.S. ( dep. commr., Punjab ) (b. 15th July, 1896).—Educ. at Chief's Coll., Lahore, and Balliol Coll., Oxford; joined the service, 12th Dec., 1921; arrived, 2nd Oct., 1922, and served in the Punjab as asst. commr.; offg. dep. commr., July, 1927; dep. commr. (provl.), Apr., 1929. SAID-UZ-ZAFAR KHAN , SAHIBZADA , M.B., late United Provs. medl. service (b. 14th Oct., 1876).—Joined the service, 19th April, 1905, as asst. surg.; prof., King George's medl. coll., July, 1914; civil surg., April, 1920; dean and prinpl., King George's medl. coll., May, 1926; on deptn. to Bhopal State from Oct., 1927; retd., Oct., 1931. SAIGAL , DEVI DAYAL ( see Devi Dayal S.). SAIN , KANWAR LALA ( see Kanwar Sain, L.), SAING , U BA , Barr., Burma Commission ( dist. and sess. judge, Burma ) (b. 9th. Nov. 1881).—Apptd. addl. and sess. judge, March, 1921; dist. and sess. judge, Dec., 1922. ST. JOHN , CECIL HENRY , late Indo-European Telegraph Dept.—Held non-gazetted appt. from 1st April, 1891, to 28th Feb., 1918; asst. supt., May, 1918; supt., Feb., 1924; engr. and electrician, Sept., 1928; retd. Oct., 1929. ST. JOHN , Sir HENRY BEAUCHAMP , K.C.I.E., C.B.E., Lt.-Col., I.A. (retd.) (b. 26th Aug., 1874).—First commn. dated 30th August, 1893; in mil. employ to May, 1899, when he was apptd. asst. commr. N.W.F. Benson Maxwell, then recorder of Penang, January 1st, 1865; employed in the registrar's department, supreme court, Penang, from 1865 to 1869; qualified as a law agent of the local bar by passing the prescribed examination in 1867; senior sworn clerk, supreme court, Singapore, February, 1869; police magistrate and commissioner of the court of requests, Penang, September, 1869; transferred in the same capacities to Malacca, February, 1870; transferred to Singapore, August, 1871, and acted as police magistrate there until April, 1872; gazetted as police magistrate and commissioner of the court of requests, province Wellesley, April, 1872; admitted a student at the Inner Temple, November, 1872; passed the general examination at Lincoln's Inn, May, 1873; resumed charge in province Wellesley, December, 1873; temporary judge of the supreme court, Penang, May, 1874; assistant government agent, province Wellesley, September, 1874; appointed deputy commissioner with the Larut field force on the occasion of the expedition to Perak to punish the murderers of the British resident, in November, 1875; acting assistant resident, Larut, August, 1876; acting assistant colonial secretary, Singapore, January, 1877; returned to Perak in February, 1877, as acting resident; acting senior magistrate, Singapore, June, 1877.

MAXWELL, WILLIAM EDWARD.—Entered the service as clerk to the recorder of Penang, Jan. 1, 1865; appointed acting senior sworn clerk to the registrar of the court of judicature, Penang division, March, 1865; confirmed in the same appointment, September, 1866; passed as a law-agent of the local bar, January, 1868; acting registrar, supreme court, Penang, November, 1868; senior sworn clerk, supreme court, Singapore, February, 1869; police magistrate, and commissioner of the court of requests, Penang, September, 1869; transferred in the same capacities to Malacca, February, 1870; administered the government at Malacca, in Aug. and Sept. in the same year during the absence of the lieutenant-governor; transferred to Singapore, August, 1871, and acted as police magistrate there until April, 1872, gazetted as police magistrate and commissioner of the court of requests, province Wellesley, April, 1872. Admitted a student at the Inner Temple, Nov. 1872; passed the general examination at Lincoln's Inn, May, 1837, and went the Oxford and Midland Circuits in the same year as marshal to Mr. Justice Honyman. sources.text: GORE, AUGUSTUS FREDERICK F.R.G.S., C.M.G. (1881).—Was acting private secretary to Sir A. Oliphant, C.B., chief justice of Ceylon, 1870; private secretary to C. Temple, Esq., second puisne judge of Ceylon, 1851, and to Sir Philip E. Wodehouse, K.C.B., when superintendent of British Honduras in 1852, and again when governor of British Guiana in 1854; acting assistant government secretary, and acting circuit stipendiary magistrate of British Guiana, 1855; was confirmed in 1857 as assistant government secretary; acted as government secretary in 1865; an inspector of prisons, 1865, and a director in 1866; was acting government secretary, chairman of the board of health, and member of the education committee, from October, 1866, until transferred to Barbados as Colonial Secretary, in March, 1867; where latterly he was a member of the executive and legislative councils; was a J.P. for the island; administered the government of St. Vincent from May to Oct., 1874; and of Grenada from March to May, 1876. Militia services.—Captain in the militia of British Guiana, 1856; military secretary, 1865, and adjutant-general, 1866; when transferred to Barbados in 1867; received a commission as military secretary, and in 1868 acted as adjutant-general; present rank, lieut.-colonel; lieut.-governor Tobago, 1877; lieut.-governor St. Vincent, 1880.

sources.text: PINE, SIR BENJAMIN CHILLEY CAMPBELL PINE. KNT. BACHEL. (Creat. 1856), K.C.M.G. (1871).—Educated at Trin. Coll., Camb., B.A. 1834, M.A. 1840; called to the bar, Gray's Inn, 1841; Queen's advocate at Sierra Leone, 1841; acting governor there, 1848; accompanied Capt. Monypenny, R.N., to the Sherbro river, and destroyed a strong stockaded fort, from which outrages had been committed on British trading vessels. In 1849 again proceeded to Sherbro, with a detachment of troops, and put an end to the civil war which had ravaged the country for years; lieut.-governor of Natal, 1849; 1851 received the thanks of her majesty's government for the measures he took to preserve peace in the colony during the Kaffir war; in 1855 led a force of mounted volunteers against the Amabaca tribe, numbering 2,000 men, and completely enforced their submission; governor and commander-in-chief Gold Coast, 1856; lieut.-governor of St. Kitts, May, 1859; is author of some articles in the Encyclopedia Britannica on the "African Colonies;" acting governor, Antigua, 1866; governor-in-chief, Leeward Islands, Feb., 1869; created K.C.M.G. for his services in connection with the confederation of the Leeward Islands; lieut.-governor of Natal, 1873, until 1875; when he retired on pension.
